reason: The verse boasts of turning the worlds to red gold (செம்பொன் னாக்குவோம்), a transmutation claim; it says nothing about ingesting metal preparations, so the contamination finding shares only the metals topic.

The poet says he knew the clarity of the Parabrahman form the guru taught (பரப்பிரம சொரூபத்தின் தெளிவறிந்தேன்); this is a mystical-realisation topic, but nothing in it describes loss of self-sense that the finding could test.

The verse uses vivid reminders of death (காலன்வருமுன்னே, ஊரார்சுடுமுன்னே) to urge turning to the Lord, implying death-awareness drives religious commitment; mortality-salience research bears on exactly that effect, but it is contested and the verse states it only as exhortation.
The verse is about the five syllables calling back the breath (வாயுவை) through the doorless gate; nothing concerns microbes in the body.

The verse promises siddhi (சித்தி) and dancing powers when practice is done on auspicious lunar days; the psi failure concerns lab precognition, so it touches only the general topic of claimed paranormal powers.
A cipher verse on breath (வாயு) between sun and moon at the gate; it has nothing to do with gravity-related collapse experiments.
A devotional confession that the world appeared false and the Lord alone true (யாவையுமெனக்குப் பொய்யெனத்தோன்றி); nothing about anaesthesia or microtubules.
Worship of Guhan and the elephant-faced god at left and right (இடம்வலம்); nothing about pulse reading.
Binding kundalini by vaasi (குண்டலி வாசியினால்) is a yogic breath cipher; loving-kindness meditation is unrelated.

The four inner instruments and five senses becoming one (நாலுவகைக்கரண, புலனைந்துமொன்றாய்) shares the topic of integrated bodily-sense awareness with the insula finding, but the verse is a spiritual state, not a claim about interoception.
The verse longs to throw off the filthy body (ஊத்தைச் சடம்); it says nothing about mind-wandering or happiness.
A devotional wish to see the god's earrings and matted hair (மகரங், செஞ்சடை); unrelated to nostril breathing and blood pressure.
The verse is about rock salt (கல்லுப்பு) and its inner meaning; mercury is not mentioned, so the mercury-toxicity finding does not apply.
A lament over a maimed, blind body weakened by base food (ஈனப் புசிப்பு); it makes no claim about gut microbes or the brain.

The verse boasts of forge work and making gold (பொன்னை யாக்குவோம், கருமா னுலை); metal-working alchemy shares the metals topic with the contamination finding, but nothing is said about medicines taken by mouth.
The verse says those who call the absolute 'breath' (மூச்சு) or 'silence' do not know its name; the word breath is incidental to any claim about breathing physiology.
The verse warns against giving room to desire (விரும்பாசை) and being bound by bodily pain; it shares the topic of desire and wellbeing with hedonic adaptation but makes no claim about set points.
Sky, grove and the fruit the elephant ate (வேழம் உண்டகனி) are riddle images; nothing about perception as prediction.

The verse says perception showed the non-existent as existing and hid what exists (இல்லனவுளவா யுள்ளனகாணா); likening that to perception as a constructed guess takes a generous reading of a metaphysical claim about the world's falsity.

The verse describes firing a red calx (செந்தூரம்) that makes the nine metals yield (நவலோகந்தான், வேதை), a transmutation claim; the finding on metal-laced remedies shares the topic but the verse does not claim ingestion here.

The verse claims a practice makes the body not perish (உடல் மாயாதல்லவோ); the ageing-hallmarks finding, that no hallmark of ageing has been reversed in humans, is evidence against a deathless body, though the practice itself is in cipher (காசாம்வேரு, வாயாற்று).
The verse lists kinds of silence (மோனம்) and self-knowers; meditative stillness is the shared topic with the speculative predictive-loosening model, but no specific claim is made.

The verse sets the mind at the suzhumunai when sun and moon exchange (பரிதிமதி யிரண்டு மாறி); reading sun and moon as the two nostrils is a cipher gloss, so the link to nostril lateralization is topic only.
The verse says even mounting the breath (வாசியில் ஏறினாலும்) will not bring the sky-thing; it shares the breath-practice topic with the HRV finding but makes no physiological claim.
The verse names the left channel as moon and the right as sun (இடைகலை, பின்கலை) and urges holding breath in the sushumna; it does not claim the alternation that the nasal-cycle finding describes.
A wish to stand in the sushumna between ida and pingala (இடைபிங் கலைநடுவே); the channels are a yogic scheme and no claim about one-nostril effects is made.
A satire of ritual worship with copper vessels and incense (புட்பபூசை); nothing about Siddha decoctions or trials.
The verse urges leaving women who speak lies (மடமாதரைவிட்டு) out of revulsion at lust; craving is the shared topic, but there is no claim about wanting versus liking.
The light beyond time (காலா காலங் கடந்திடும் சோதி) is a mystical image; the word time is incidental to circadian biology.
A devotional verse on Om Namasivaya as strength (உரம்); no claim about ageing.
The five-headed serpent's poison cured by the Lord (ஐந்துதலை நாகம், விடந்தீர்க்கும்) is an image for the senses; nothing about lifespan limits.
The verse says knowing the soham seed makes alchemy (வாதம்) sky-going; alchemy is the shared topic with metal-contaminated remedies, but no claim about taking metals is made.

The verse claims that cutting the sedge in the root pond lets one live as a child (பாலனாகி வாழலாம்); the means is a cipher, and voluntary autonomic control shares only the topic of bodily mastery by practice.

The verse prescribes exhaling by pingala and inhaling on the left, then holding (இரேசகம், பூரகம், கும்பி) to reach the Siva-gaze; the finding concerns physiological lateralization claims, which the verse does not make.

The verse claims salt (உப்பு) hardens the body for aeons (காய மிதுவலுத்து); it is an alchemical longevity claim, but salt here is a cipher and mercury is not named, so the mercury-toxicity finding shares only the topic.
The Lord beyond speech and mind, subtle among the subtle (நுண்ணியரில் நுண்ணியன்); no claim about quantum states in the brain.
Self-knowers hide themselves while the ignorant show off (தன்னையறிந்து); nothing about adverse meditation experiences.
The verse claims the sixty-four arts come to hand (சஷ்டிவித்தை கைவசமாம்); a general claim of powers, which the lab psi-replication finding touches only by topic.
The crow-sage claims to have lived on earth through crores of yugas (யுகங்கள் தோறும்); psi replication failures concern precognition, so the link is only the topic of paranormal claims.
Yesterday and tomorrow as remembering and forgetting (நேற்றென்றுநாளையென்று) is a devotional theme; no link to brain structure after mindfulness training.
